definitions.gloss: groove; the rhythmic feel or swing of music
definitions.explanation: The infectious rhythmic feel of a piece of music — the sense of momentum and swing that makes listeners want to move. Borrowed from English 'groove.'

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{曲|きょく}→曲：09881_kyoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧グルーブ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦バンド→バンド：05508_bando⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧グルーブ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}って→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦{踊|おど}る→踊る：01250_odoru⟧。
examples.english: I dance, riding the band's groove.

examples.japanese: ⟦ベース→ベース：08762_beesu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦ドラム→ドラム：04463_doramu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|う}み{出|だ}す→生み出す：10423_umidasu⟧グルーブ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{心地|ここち}よい→心地よい：12515_kokochiyoi⟧。
examples.english: The groove created by the bass and drums feels great.

notes:
Borrowed from English 'groove.' Refers to the rhythmic feel and swing of music rather than its literal beat — the quality that makes a performance feel alive. Also written グルーヴ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- グルーブ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧: to have groove
- グルーブ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧: to get into the groove
- グルーブ⟦{感|かん}→〜感：28578_kan⟧: a sense of groove

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{拍|はく}→拍：30066_haku⟧ / ⟦ビート→ビート：06590_biito⟧: beat — the underlying pulse; groove is the feel built on top of it
- ⟦リズム→リズム：04746_rizumu⟧: rhythm — the pattern of sounds in time; broader than groove
